A1.justification: While I appreciate the compromises reflected in this specification, and support moving towards more proactive student support, my reservations remain regarding reliance on predictive modelling at all. Implementation *must* be contingent on robust ongoing monitoring for bias, complete data transparency with opt-out options for students, and substantial investment in universal support systems. Furthermore, ethical oversight should ensure the model genuinely serves student wellbeing, not institutional efficiency.

A2.justification: While I appreciate the group's attempt at compromise, and support many aspects of this specification (especially prioritizing fairness and limiting sensitive data use), I remain deeply concerned about relying on predictive modelling *at all*. My support is contingent on robust safeguards – continuous monitoring for bias, transparent algorithms accessible to scrutiny, and most importantly, a demonstrable commitment to universal support services that address systemic issues rather than simply identifying individual 'risks'. The model should augment, not replace, human-centered advising.
